system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What Wattlebridge should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, supported by diligence and risk allocation; keep fundamental, title, tax, specific indemnity and fraud liabilities outside this general cap. | **Reject; seek a substantially higher general cap and clear separate regimes**, because AUD 4.8m may not cover material business-wide warranty breaches. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | Lower de minimis and a smaller tipping basket (or deductible basket only as a fallback), with aggregation rules that prevent claim fragmentation or circumvention. | **Counter with lower thresholds and a tipping basket**, because the proposed deductible leaves the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 even after the basket is crossed. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within **18 months**; Seller says any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period (at least through the relevant statutory limitation period where appropriate), with distinct periods for tax, title, fundamental warranties and indemnities; no blanket extension of the general limit to all Claims. | **Reject the blanket rule and negotiate separate, longer survival periods**, because latent, tax and other claims may emerge after 18 months. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties. | Separate, higher or uncapped liability and longer survival for capacity, ownership, title and authority; clarify treatment of specific indemnities. | **Reject; carve fundamental and title claims out of the general cap and time bar**, because defects in ownership or authority undermine the transaction itself. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is stated. | Expressly preserve liability for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation (including relevant attribution protections), outside caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance restrictions, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express fraud carve-out**, because otherwise the Seller’s broad limitations could be argued to restrict remedies for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire indexed data room as at 22 September 2026, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair, sufficiently detailed disclosure against each warranty; limit general disclosure to identified documents or matters that are reasonably apparent, and exclude undifferentiated data-room/public-record disclosure. | **Reject blanket general disclosure and require particularised disclosure**, because it could qualify warranties by reference to a large, unreviewable body of material. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No imputed or constructive knowledge bar; at most, narrowly defined actual knowledge of specified Buyer personnel after express written disclosure, without limiting fraud or specific indemnity claims. | **Reject the proposed qualifier**, because “discoverable” knowledge makes the warranty package depend on subjective diligence and an effectively unlimited search obligation. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty written consent. DD-002 shows about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and consent conditions; no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | Completion conditional on final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all contractual conditions, obtained before Completion; Buyer termination or other agreed remedy if absent. | **Make valid consent and condition satisfaction a completion condition**, because Bluefen is material and a mere consent letter may not satisfy clause 11.3. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. DD-003 says not repaid and no final security discharge is in the room. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller proceeds or agreed funds flow, with lender payoff evidence, release of all security and discharge deliverables as completion conditions. | **Do not accept post-Completion release; require simultaneous repayment and discharge**, because Buyer would otherwise acquire the Company with debt and secured assets outstanding. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are not itemised in the draft funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. On-costs are unspecified. | Identify gross bonuses and all payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs; allocate them to Seller or account for them as debt/debt-like items or a price adjustment, with payment mechanics and releases documented. | **Resolve and fund the full bonus and on-cost exposure at Completion**, because it is triggered by the transaction, omitted from funds flow and may exceed AUD 420,000 including on-costs. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 conditions transfer of Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open but is not bank verification, and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the room. | A specific, uncapped or separately capped indemnity covering payment, ownership, transfer/assignment and any resulting loss; verified cleared payment and effective IP assignment/transfer as Completion deliverables. | **Expand the indemnity and require evidence of payment and transfer**, because paying one amount alone may not satisfy the contractual conditions for transferring the materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls DD-006 preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure does not establish access, scope or notification obligations. | Complete investigation and incident particulars; assess applicable notification obligations, preserve evidence and remediate; specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident losses and liabilities, with appropriate disclosure and completion protections. | **Treat as an unresolved specific risk, not dismissed as immaterial**, because the possible exposure of about 1,240 records and notification status remain unknown. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008 and DD-011 together do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Obtain the contracts and renewal terms; determine termination, accrual and commitment status, and treat any unusual, unavoidable or unpaid pre-Completion amounts as debt-like or a specific adjustment. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course label without verification**, because timing and contractual commitment may leave the Buyer with material liabilities or locked-in spend. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Distinct negotiated regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and other claims, with appropriate caps, thresholds, survival periods and remedies for each. | **Reject the all-Claims approach and expressly separate categories**, because applying general warranty limits across the board can unintentionally dilute specific protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register recording it as holder of 100%; Seller says title is evidenced by that register. | Verify issued capital, register, constitution and corporate records, and obtain executed transfer instruments and evidence of good title free of encumbrances at Completion; retain robust title warranties. | **Treat DD-012 as a source, not conclusive verification**, because the disclosure itself does not establish the Buyer’s independent verification or delivery of effective transfer documents. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP positions settled under the general regime. | Negotiate explicit tax and IP warranty scope, separate caps and survival periods, and any identified specific tax/IP indemnities; resolve these expressly in the SPA rather than by implication. | **Keep tax and IP open until expressly documented**, because the Seller’s assertion does not specify the protections or resolve their treatment under the proposed general limitations. |

These are negotiation recommendations based on the supplied Seller materials; confirm them against the full SPA, due diligence record and agreed transaction mechanics before marking up.
=== END ADVICE ===
